chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala' said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the garment for the muhrim (one in ihram) that saffron touches, then is washed, so he said, 'There is no harm with it if its scent disappears, and even if the whole thing was dyed, if it leans towards whiteness, there is no harm with it.' And sleeping on dyed carpets is disliked. He narrated that.

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: for the one in ihram (holy state)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a garment stained with saffron for someone in ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the prohibition of scented garments and the mere presence of color in ihram, establishing that saffron-stained clothing is permissible once its fragrance dissipates. The Imam’s ruling highlights the principle that the prohibition targets the scent itself rather than the dye, provided the color does not become too vivid. Furthermore, it extends this leniency to sleeping on dyed carpets, noting that while not strictly forbidden, it is considered disliked (makruh) to maintain a state of ritual purity and simplicity.
